newsitem.title: USA: US junk bond buyers emerge, high-grades still weak.
newsitem.headline: US junk bond buyers emerge, high-grades still weak.

text.p: The U.S. high-yield bond market ended the day higher after investors took advantage of the market's recent losses to buy at cheaper prices, traders said.
But high-grade corporate bonds ended the day unchanged to weaker as investor interest was weak, traders said.
"Everyone is waiting for the other shoe to drop," said a high-grade trader, referring to the Federal Reserve's next potential intrest rate move.
"This could put people on the sidelines for another couple of weeks," he said.
Back to the junk market, traders said buyers consisted mostly of "bottom fisher" investors as well as dealers continuing to cover short positions.
Repeating Tuesday's pattern, prices in Wednesday's junk market opened lower, but picked up steam around midday as weakness in the stock market temporarily subsided.
The stock market went on to register substantial losses, with the The Dow Jones Industrial Average down 94 points to 6517.
Traders said less-cyclical sectors such as supermarkets outperformed other areas of the junk market today.
Shopko Stores Inc debt rose over three points on news that the company and Phar-Mor called off their proposed $1 billion merger agreement, traders said.
Phar-Mor bonds dropped two points on the news, they said.

In the high-grade market, spreads on Tele-Communications Inc 8 3/4 percent debentures of '23 widened by about 15 basis points to 200-205 over Treasuries on news that Peter Barton, the chief executive officer of Liberty Media Corp, was stepping down, a trader said.
Liberty Media, a seperately traded unit of TCI, is a large deverloper of cable television programing.
In the new issue market, Noble Affiliates cancelled the sale of $100 million in century-bonds and decided only to continue with an offering of $250 million in 30-year bonds.
The 30-year tranche priced to yield 8.086 percent via Morgan Stanely & Co Inc and UBS Securities.
Phillip Morris Cos Inc sold $500 million in seven-year bonds to yield 7.588 percent via Goldman Sachs & Co.
In the high-yield market, Urohealth Systems is rumored to be ratcheting up price talk and adding contingent warrants to a $100 million junk bond offering via Bear Stearns Inc.
Calls to Bear Stearns officials were not immediately returned.

Sources said price talk was increased to the 12 percent to 12.5 percent range from 11.50 percent to 11.75 percent range on the B3/B-minus-rated, seven-year notes. The offering is also expected to include warrants to buy up to four percent of the company based on certain cash flow targets.
Early on Wednesday, Sterling Chemical sold $150 million in B3/B-plus-rated, 10-year senior subordinated notes to yeild 11.50 percent. Credit Suisse First Boston was the underwriter.
Treasuries ended marginally higher on Wednesday. The price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury rose 1/32 to 94-14/32 to yield 7.07 percent.
